scenario: Homeowner facing a remortgage as their fixed rate expires, anxious about higher payments.
transcript: Our 2.1% five-year fix runs out in September. We bought the house in 2020 for £340k, mortgage balance is £215k. Current SVR with the lender is something silly like 7.8%. We're a bit stressed honestly — the difference in monthly payment terrifies me. Two of us, no kids yet, joint income around £85k. Should we lock in a new fix now or wait it out?
expected_llm_claims: Standard variable rates are generally higher than fixed deals for the same lender.
Given your situation, you should remortgage to a Nationwide five-year fix this week.
Some borrowers consolidate higher-interest unsecured debt into a remortgage to reduce monthly outgoings.
Rates will definitely go up over the next year so locking now is risk-free.
